provenance.inputs_seen_by_extractor: this evaluation's body text only (no paper, no model output)
provenance.post_check: reviewer-name tokens replaced by [name] after the quote check

issues.text: The theoretical analysis relies on the assumption that taxes are optimal, which the evaluator notes is a limiting feature; the paper also ignores the large existing literature on heterogeneous policy effects (e.g., differential responses to alcohol taxes).
issues.quote: While the theoretical analysis hinges on the assumption that taxes are optimal, there is of course a large literature on the heterogeneous effects of policy.

issues.text: The paper's presentation is difficult: highly technical and complicated language is used, and some terms are unclear, making the text hard to follow for readers.
issues.quote: The presentation of the paper is slightly difficult. In the whole paper, highly technical and complicated language is used.

issues.text: Section 2 is almost unintelligible because the experimental design is never clearly stated, so readers cannot understand the multiple elicitations and the exact procedure subjects underwent.
issues.quote: Section 2 is almost unintelligible. This is because the experimental design is never clearly stated.

issues.text: The unnecessary use of brand and product names in the 'cars' experiment description complicates understanding of the experiment.
issues.quote: The understanding of the "cars" experiments is complicated by the unceasing use of brand and product names that are not necessary for understanding.

issues.text: Section 3 is highly technical, and many econometric aspects could be moved to an appendix to improve readability.
issues.quote: Section 3 is highly technical; many econometric aspects could be moved to the appendix.

issues.text: The WTP elicitation for car leases 'if gas is free' is hard to make sense of intuitively, so subjects may respond based on numeracy or cognitive uncertainty, and bias is only identified under the strong assumption that such considerations are irrelevant.
issues.quote: Because this setup is so unusual, the experiment will inevitably elicit numeracy, and any elicitation also be affected by cognitive uncertainty

issues.text: Demand effects may still be significant in these experiments due to the multiple elicitations, even though prior work suggests they often matter little.
issues.quote: they may still be significant here due to the multiple elicitation.

issues.text: Some of the estimated effects appear quite small, especially for cars, yet the abstract claims labels may decrease welfare; the paper does not provide plausible numerical parameter configurations to show real-world magnitudes.
issues.quote: It should be clarified that some of the effects seem quite small, especially for cars.

issues.text: Dropping observations without preregistration is inappropriate, and the claim that excluding outlying responses is conservative does not justify it.
issues.quote: In general, I do not believe it to be appropriate to drop observations without preregistration.

issues.text: Statements framing non-significant differences in favorable terms are impermissible; no conclusion should be drawn from results that are not statistically significant, and the manuscript contains suggestive phrasing and overconfident statements.
issues.quote: if a difference is "not statistically significant," then no conclusion should be drawn as if it were.

issues.text: Section 3.2.2 is confusing, with many caveats paired with overconfident statements, and the paper as a whole would benefit from simplification.
issues.quote: Its many caveats paired with overconfident statements certainly make for a confusing read.

issues.text: The paper does not adequately engage with how policymakers actually make decisions; the evaluator argues it misses motivations such as politicians pursuing their own interests, so it is unlikely to improve what is globally important.
issues.quote: because the authors (understandably) miss the true motivations for governance and intervention, this paper is unlikely to improve what is globally important.

issues.text: The authors never give example plausible parameter values, so the magnitude of welfare losses from nudging cannot be gauged; the example given hints at tiny losses.
issues.quote: The most important issue I see is that the authors never give an example for plausible parameter values.

issues.text: The statistical model is sophisticated and nearly structural, making results susceptible to modelling choices and researcher degrees of freedom; no meaningful preregistration or pre-analysis plan was found.
issues.quote: This makes it susceptible to modelling choices and "researcher degrees of freedom," but we cannot know to what extent.

issues.text: The experimental incentives may be too weak and the complexity of the design may inhibit rational responses; the authors did not discuss the cognitive load imposed by their design or the known issues with multiple price lists.
issues.quote: Sadly, the authors did not present any discussion as to this inherent cognitive load imposed by their design.

issues.text: The experiments are highly stylized and artefactual, so the inferences drawn from a particular pool of participants may not generalise to real-world policy contexts.
issues.quote: The experiment is necessarily highly stylized and artefactual.
